newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to sell 60 mln Gulf Bank shares.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to sell 60 mln Gulf Bank shares.

text.p: The Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA) plans to sell 60 million shares of its Gulf Bank stake for 27 million dinars ($89.4 million) in a public offering in February, bankers said on Thursday.
"The Authority wants to sell 60 million shares for a total of 27 million dinars in a public subscription," said a banker.
The offering is the second phase of plan to shed most of the state's stake in the bank under a wide-ranging three-year-old privatisation programme.
Earlier in January KIA, the state investment arm, sold 30 million shares of its 97-million-share initial stake at Gulf Bank for 17.1 million dinars in an auction.
Total Gulf Bank subscribed shares amount to 781.7 million.

"The subscription price has been set at 450 fils each," said a banker. There are 1,000 fils to the dinar. The share, which fetched 570 fils in the auction against a starting price of 510 fils, closed on 500 fils on Wednesday.
KIA has set three million shares as a maximum limit for each subscriber, said a banker.
Gulf Bank has reported a rise in 1996 net profit to 31.3 million dinars from 25.5 million dinars the previous year.
It announced a 31 percent dividend distribution -- 31 fils per share -- which still requires approval by the general assembly.
Kuwait's Central Bank has allowed Gulf Bank, established in 1960, to buy up to 10 percent of its own shares at a maximum value of 25 million dinars over six months.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can take part in the offering.
